items.text: Your college fest committee needs volunteers. Which role do you sign up for without hesitation?

options.label: Set up and manage the stage equipment and sound system
Research and design the event theme with data from past fests
Coordinate all volunteers, make sure everyone has a role
Promote the fest on social media and design creatives
Handle registrations, budget tracking, and vendor payments

items.text: You have a major exam in 3 weeks and a club event happening this weekend. What do you actually do?

options.label: Skip the event, start studying immediately with a fixed schedule
Attend the event but study every other day leading up to the exam
Attend the event and cram the night before the exam
Delegate your club responsibilities to someone else so you can prepare

items.text: You get two internship offers. Offer A pays ₹25,000/month in a field you find boring. Offer B pays ₹8,000 in a field that genuinely interests you. What do you pick?

options.label: Offer A. Money now is more important
Offer B. The learning matters more than the pay at this stage
Negotiate Offer B's pay upward before deciding
Ask family, then decide based on their input

items.text: A friend describes their startup idea to you. What's the first thing your mind does?

options.label: Start calculating if the numbers actually work — market size, costs, margins
Think about how to tell the story to investors or customers
Visualise the product — what it looks like, how it flows
Immediately think about the team — who's needed, what roles
Ask whether this idea actually solves a real human problem

items.text: You're given free time and a small budget of ₹5,000. You most naturally…

options.label: Start a small resale or service business to turn a profit
Use it to attend a skill workshop or online course
Organise a community event or help someone in need
Spend it on art supplies, music gear, or creative tools

items.text: Your professor gives a completely unconventional assignment — no rules, just 'submit something meaningful'. You feel…

options.label: Excited. This is when I do my best work
Curious but a little anxious — you'll work through it
Frustrated. You prefer clear guidelines and rubrics
Indifferent. You'll just do the minimum needed to pass

items.text: When someone asks you 'what do you want to do after graduation?', you typically…

options.label: Have a clear, specific answer with a plan already in motion
Have a few options you're seriously considering but haven't decided
Give a vague answer because you genuinely haven't thought deeply about it
Get anxious — you worry you're behind everyone else

items.text: You have to explain a complex topic to your class. You instinctively create…

options.label: A visual diagram, infographic, or sketch
A well-structured written explanation with examples
A live demonstration or hands-on activity
A story or analogy that makes it relatable
A spreadsheet or data breakdown

items.text: Your ideal study or work environment is…

options.label: A busy café or co-working space with ambient noise
A quiet room, alone, with no distractions
A small group of 2-3 people you trust
Wherever the deadline pressure pushes you

items.text: Which of these statements feels most true for you right now?

options.label: I know exactly what I'm good at and I build on those strengths
I'm still figuring out where my strengths really lie
I feel like others are more capable than me in most areas
I'm good at many things but nothing stands out

items.text: You're watching a documentary. You're most drawn to content about…

options.label: How diseases spread and how the body fights back
How a startup went from zero to billion-dollar company
How ancient civilisations built structures we still can't replicate
How a director creates emotional impact through filmmaking
How policy changes affect millions of people across a country

items.text: A teammate is consistently not pulling their weight on a group project. You…

options.label: Confront them directly and clearly explain the impact on the team
Take on their work to avoid conflict and keep the project on track
Talk to them privately, try to understand what's going wrong
Report it to the professor or group leader

items.text: When learning something new, you absorb it best when you…

options.label: Actually do it — build it, perform it, make it with your hands
Read about it deeply and take detailed notes
Watch a video or observe someone doing it first
Discuss it with someone else to test your understanding
Map it out in a diagram or framework before diving in

items.text: A random conversation at a family event gives you an unexpected opportunity in a field you'd never considered. You…

options.label: Get excited and follow up on it immediately
Think about it seriously before making any move
Dismiss it — it doesn't fit your current plan
Mention it to family to see if they approve first

items.text: You're at your most energised and 'in flow' when you are…

options.label: Teaching, mentoring, or explaining something to someone
Solving a puzzle, debugging a problem, or figuring out how something works
Creating something — writing, designing, composing
Persuading people or negotiating a deal
Executing a process efficiently and getting things done correctly

items.text: Before a high-stakes presentation or performance, you typically feel…

options.label: Calm and prepared — pressure is just part of the process
Nervous but it pushes you to perform better
Extremely anxious — it significantly affects your performance
Indifferent — you don't overthink these things

items.text: Which of these describes why you want to be successful in your chosen career?

options.label: I want to become genuinely good at something that matters to me
I want financial security and a stable, respected life
I want my family to be proud of what I've achieved
I want to solve a real problem or contribute to something bigger

items.text: Which of these tasks would you actually enjoy doing as part of your regular work?

options.label: Analysing large datasets to find patterns or insights
Managing and coordinating a team's workflow and timelines
Designing visuals, user interfaces, or creative content
Conducting lab work, experiments, or technical analysis
Writing reports, policies, documentation, or proposals

items.text: When researching a major life decision (college, career, city to move to), you…

options.label: Go deep — read everything, talk to people in that field, build a spreadsheet
Do a quick search, trust your gut, and move on
Ask people you trust and mostly go with their advice
Delay until the deadline forces a decision

items.text: Which of these elective subjects would you have genuinely loved in school?

options.label: Music theory and composition
Environmental science and ecology
Physical education, sports science, or dance
Computer science and programming
Psychology and human behaviour

items.text: You have a business idea you genuinely believe in. The only way to test it is to spend ₹20,000 of your savings. You…

options.label: Do it immediately — the only way to know is to try
Build a scaled-down version to test first with minimal investment
Wait until you have more certainty before spending money
Look for a co-founder to share the financial risk

items.text: Your parents strongly prefer you pursue a specific career. You want something different. You…

options.label: Follow your own path and explain your reasoning to them over time
Try to find a middle ground that satisfies both sides
Agree to their preference to avoid conflict, even if unhappy
Delay the decision and hope the situation resolves itself

items.text: You're asked to rate yourself honestly. Which statement is most accurate?

options.label: I understand my strengths, weaknesses, values, and motivations clearly
I know some things about myself but a lot is still unclear
I find it difficult to reflect on myself — I just go with the flow
I understand myself but I often doubt what I know

items.text: On a group project, which role do you naturally drift into?

options.label: The one who motivates the group and keeps morale high
The one who structures the plan and assigns tasks
The one who generates the most ideas and challenges assumptions
The one who executes and gets the actual work done
The one who researches and makes sure decisions are evidence-based

items.text: 10 years from now, the version of you that feels most fulfilled is someone who…

options.label: Has built something — a company, product, or system others depend on
Is recognised as an expert or leader in their field
Has made a visible, tangible difference in people's lives
Has creative work in the world that reflects who they are
Has financial freedom, stability, and professional respect
